Subject: Private VPC Safe-Stitch Upgrade: pin window and evacuation rehearsal

Hi Julia / Acme OPS team,

Were preparing the private VPC upgrade for your cluster (c-acme-01) and want to lock in a short maintenance window and a rehearsal for rollback/evacuation. Key goals: pin the inference runtime to 2025-04 build for the maintenance window, run a canary evacuate (2 nodes), validate KV cache rehydration, and confirm BGP quiesce/restore timing with your NetOps.

High-level plan (attachment: redwood_private_safe-stitch_runbook_v1.pdf):
- Maintenance window: Fri Aug 29, 02:00-03:30 UTC (target low traffic)
- Preflight: KV drain on canary nodes, metric snapshot, perf baseline capture (T-48h to T-2h)
- Patch order: control plane -> router agents -> runtime nodes -> canaries -> remainder
- Pinning: pin model-serving runtime to 2025-04-build (no auto-upgrades during window)
- Rollback triggers: >3% 5m error-rate increase sustained for 10m, token-latency p95 >2x baseline, or failed KV rehydrate on >1 canary
- Evacuation rehearsal: warm standby routing, redirect 10% traffic to hosted fallback if needed, full canary drain rehearsal at T+30m

Requesting: confirmation on the window, contact for BGP changes (NetOps), and a short DocuSign approval for maintenance access. Ive attached the runbook and a simplified network stitch diagram.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: redwood_private_safe-stitch_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB), vpc_network_stitch_diagram_v3.png (PNG, 340KB)

Thanks for the detailed planthis looks solid. A couple of asks from our side:
1) Could we shift the maintenance window two hours earlier (00:00-01:30 UTC)? That reduces overlap with our batch settlement jobs.
2) We need the runbook to include an explicit list of service-account actions and the minimum set of IAM scopes your engineers will use. Compliance needs that to sign off.
3) For hosted fallback: we need SLA text confirming token retention and encryption boundaries while traffic is redirected.

We can sign DocuSign once the IAM appendix and SLA snippet are in the runbook.

Diego / team,

Ill own runtime gating and canary checks. A few operational clarifications:
- Canary size: 2 runtime pods (gpu-a2) draining sequence: 1) stop new sessions 2) flush KV prefix 3) wait for 30s idle 4) power-cycle
- KV rehydrate test: synthetic traffic that replays last-24h prefixes; success = <5% miss rate after 90s
- Fallback: hosted fallback will receive parity traffic only for reads (no writes). We need to ensure clients are aware of read-only semantics during rollback.

Ill update the runbook with the gating steps and include the IAM actions you requested, Diego.

-SoojIN
Soojin Lee
Runtime Reliability, Redwood Inference

Quick notes from runtime/quantization side:
- Order of node updates: control plane -> router agents -> runtime (model) nodes -> aux services. Applying quantized kernel pack should be after runtime node reboot, not before; thats caused past startup jitter.
- Canary verification: verify tokenization/embedding parity on a 2000-sample test set. If >1% semantic drift observed (by our eval harness), trigger immediate rollback.
- Version pin: 2025-04 is fine. We should capture a container image digest and pin it in the deployment manifest so autoscaling doesnt accidentally pull latest.

Ill add the test harness commands to the canary checklist and push a PR to the runbook.

—Rishi
Applied ML / Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference

Diego et al.,

Adding operational abort criteria and observability thresholds (short list for runbook):
- Health checks: 1m node heartbeat missing -> abort
- API error rate: >3% 5m with alert escalation to on-call -> abort and auto-evacuate canaries
- KV rehydrate: failure to reach <5% miss rate in 2m -> rollback to pinned image and rehydrate attempt on warm spare
- Network: BGP withdrawal lasting >90s during the cutover -> escalate to Acme NetOps and hold on next tranche

Also recommend we schedule a short dry-run in a staging VLAN on Thu Aug 27 (we can do a 30-min dry run focusing purely on KV drain/rehydrate and BGP quiesce). That will satisfy compliance and give Julia confidence.

Neha Kapoor
Service Reliability, Redwood Inference
